docs.title: Overview
docs.text: This is the input-specific developer guide generated for the target folder. It combines the legacy structured style (modes + architecture + workflow) and the latest runtime artifact view.

docs.title: Pipeline Stages
docs.text:
1. File scan and parser extraction
  2. Knowledge graph build (or Bevel ingest)
  3. LLM enrichment for function metadata
  4. Workflow tracing + test scenario synthesis
  5. Artifact generation (PDF/JSON/Docs)

docs.title: Core Components
docs.text:
• Parser and scanner
  • Graph builder and entity resolver
  • Metadata and route/tag assignment
  • Workflow tracer
  • PDF and docs generators
  • Debug/Autofix/Push agents

docs.title: Artifact Usage
docs.text:
• PDF report: stakeholder-ready documentation snapshot
  • Function metadata JSON: route/tags/logic per function
  • Test scenarios JSON: function/workflow examples
  • Manual + implementation guide PDFs: operational and technical references

docs.title: AST Mode (default)
docs.text:
Directly parses Python source files from the input folder and builds the graph from code structure.

python main.py --folder "C:\Users\jarvi\OneDrive\Desktop\Book syntesizer\memory_input_clean\Memory"

docs.title: Bevel Mode
docs.text:
Uses a Bevel graph export as source structure and overlays AST details for richer metadata.

python main.py --folder "C:\Users\jarvi\OneDrive\Desktop\Book syntesizer\memory_input_clean\Memory" --bevel-graph "<BEVEL_JSON_PATH>"

docs.title: When To Use
docs.text:
• Use AST mode for normal project analysis.
  • Use Bevel mode when your mentor/review flow expects Bevel graph origin.

docs.title: Workflow Objective
docs.text: Trace entry points through critical calls so documentation reflects real execution behavior.

docs.title: Quality Controls
docs.text:
• Generic phrase suppression
  • Business tag normalization
  • Entry-point-aware workflow reachability
  • Function/workflow scenario generation with negative paths
